actions.action: Check whether the soil stays wet for days, whether pots have drainage holes, and whether leaves are yellowing or stems are soft
If overwatering signs are found, fix that problem
Inspect leaf undersides and stem joints for scale or mealybugs
Inspect plants at night with a flashlight for caterpillars, slugs or snails and hand-pick any found
Move plants away from netting, railings and wind
Keep pets away from the plants
Trim torn leaves back to healthy tissue or remove mostly damaged leaves
Check soil 2 inches down before watering and water only when dry
If no pests or pet activity are found, take a close-up video of the damage

reason: The answer names chewing pests as the main cause but never mentions low humidity, so it gets only part of the diagnosis and omits the misting fix that worked, though nothing it recommends is harmful.
